review_summary: Question 10 (Alternating Currents and Medical Physics) verified with PASS across all 3 leaves (a), (b), and (c). Leaf (a) verifies the mathematical derivation of sinusoidal alternating voltage: calculating peak voltage V_0 = sqrt(2) * V_rms = sqrt(2) * 9.9 V = 14.0 V (14 V) and angular frequency omega = 2 * pi * f = 2 * pi * 50 s^-1 = 314 rad s^-1 (C1), yielding the time-dependent expression V = 14 sin(314t) (A1). Leaf (b) verifies the physical principles of gradient magnetic fields in NMRI: stating that the non-uniform field enables spatial localization of resonating nuclei (B1), explaining that the resonant Larmor precession frequency depends on magnetic field strength (B1), and noting that the calibrated/varying gradient field creates a unique magnetic field strength and resonant frequency at each point (B1). Leaf (c) verifies composite X-ray beam attenuation and decibel calculation: applying the exponential attenuation law I = I_0 * exp(-mu * x) across bone (x = 0.40 cm, mu = 2.9 cm^-1) and soft tissue (x = 1.4 cm, mu = 0.92 cm^-1) (C1 + C1), determining the transmitted intensity ratio I / I_0 = 0.0865 (C1), and converting to decibels ratio in dB = 10 * lg(0.0865) = -11 dB (A1) with hybrid numeric checking at -11 dB ± 0.5 dB. All progressive hints, step-by-step walkthroughs, marking point rubrics, deterministic checks, and taxonomy mappings are fully compliant.
